# FDG8095

> DO NOT store URI/URL data in a string.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 8.11.1 System.Uri Implementation Guidelines.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: draft

Analyzer candidate rejected: whether a string field holds a URI is told only by its name, a heuristic; CA1056 uses it for externally visible properties under FDG8091.

## From the book

When you accept a URI/URL input as a string, you should convert the string to `System.Uri` and store the instance of `System.Uri`.

```csharp
public class SomeResource {
  Uri location;
  public SomeResource(string location) {
     this.location = new Uri(location);
  }
  public SomeResource(Uri location){
    this.location = location;
 }
}
```
